What GEO is — in plain words

SEO helped you rank in a list of Google links. GEO is different: a patient types “best family dentist in Austin” or “dental implants cost near me” into ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Google AI Overviews — and the engine gives one answer, naming a few practices. If your practice is not named, that patient usually never sees you at all.

1 · You get measured

10 fixed patient prompts are run in 4 engines — ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews. For each one: were you mentioned? Were you cited? Which competitor was named instead?

2 · The signals get fixed

Google Business Profile, directory listings (Google, Yelp, Healthgrades, Zocdoc), reviews, and answer-first pages on your site — the third-party signals AI engines cite most.

3 · You get re-measured

The same 10 prompts, re-run every month, in a 1-page report. That repeat measurement — not a promise — is what you are paying for.

Honest limit, in writing: No one can guarantee an AI citation or ranking. A 2026 review by Tenpoint Labs found “no technique with a stable, longitudinal, cross-platform causal effect on discoverability,” and Ahrefs tracked 1,885 pages adding schema and found no meaningful citation uplift. AI answers also vary by wording, time and location. This service sells an audit + measured visibility tracking + fixing the signals engines cite — never a guaranteed result.

Why dentists, why one city, why now

Generic GEO is already crowded: 214 GEO agencies were counted in one pricing dataset, selling mostly to SaaS, finance and legal. GEO for dentists is thin — a search returns only a handful of dedicated pages (Raftwise, DentalMention, and an AACD guide sponsored by Rosemont Media) — and no source found sells a sub-$1,000/mo dental GEO retainer as a packaged product.

Open question: no exact count of “GEO-for-dentists agencies” exists. The “handful” claim is directional — based on that search returning ~4 dedicated pages vs 214 agencies overall — not a census.

That is why this service is deliberately narrow: independent practices, in one metro at a time, at a price far below the market (see Pricing).

Questions dentists ask

Is GEO just SEO with a new name?

No. SEO ranks you in a list of links. GEO is about being named and cited inside the AI’s single answer. The work overlaps (your profile, reviews and pages matter for both), but the measurement is different: 10 fixed patient prompts, 4 AI engines, mentioned / cited / competitor-named — recorded and re-run monthly. Note also: Google says existing SEO practices remain relevant and special AI files, schema or chunking are not required (via DentalMention) — so anyone selling you a magic file is selling you something Google says you don’t need.

Can you guarantee ChatGPT will recommend us?

No — and you should not buy from anyone who does. See the honest-limit box above: no stable causal technique has been demonstrated, and AI answers vary by wording, time and location. What you buy is measurement, the fixes to the signals engines cite (85% of mentions come from third-party sources, per AirOps via Virayo), and a monthly re-test that proves or disproves progress.

What do you need from us?

Access to review drafts (you approve every clinical claim — nothing about your credentials, prices or outcomes is invented), your Google Business Profile details, and 30 minutes for the audit call. Dental advertising rules vary by US state, which is another reason your practice reviews everything before it is published.

Why is it $795 when agencies charge $6,850?

Because this is one specialist, one vertical, one metro at a time, using free tools (free ChatGPT / Perplexity / Gemini, Google Business Profile, Search Console, Sheets, Loom free tier) — no agency overhead and no paid GEO platform in the cost base. The market median is $6,850/mo (First Page Sage, with the seller-source caveat above); $795 is a deliberate penetration price, and it will not be discounted below $495 / $795.

How many clients do you take?

Few, on purpose. An audit takes ~4–5 hours and a retainer ~6–8 hours per client per month, so solo capacity caps at roughly 12–15 retainers before quality breaks. That cap is stated plainly rather than hidden.

What if it doesn’t work for us?

Each Retainer term is just 30 days. At the end of a term the plan pauses automatically — if you don’t want to continue, simply don’t pay the next Payoneer invoice and the plan stays paused. And you keep the audit, the drafts and the templates either way. There is no published audit-to-retainer conversion rate for dental GEO, and no published figure for how much an offshore seller’s close rate differs from a US seller’s — both are open questions in the research behind this service, stated here rather than papered over.
